operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of cancellation request statuses for the authenticated user.

This endpoint provides access to cancellation request information based on user role. Customers can view their own cancellation request history including statuses (pending, approved, rejected), reasons provided, and timestamps. Sellers can view pending cancellation requests that require their action on products they sell, enabling them to approve or reject customer requests.

The operation respects data isolation rules - customers only see their own requests while sellers see pending requests for their products. Response includes essential status information optimized for listing displays without loading full cancellation request details.

The endpoint supports pagination to handle large result sets efficiently. Results are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) by default.

Soft Delete: The system uses soft delete for cancellation requests via the deleted_at field. Only active (non-deleted) cancellation requests are returned to maintain audit trails while hiding logically deleted records. This aligns with the ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests schema's soft delete capability.

Related operations: GET /cancellation-requests/{id} for detailed view of specific cancellation request. POST /cancellation-requests to submit new cancellation request.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests table with role-based filtering.

For customer users: Filter where customer_id equals authenticated user ID. Return request_status, reason, created_at, updated_at fields paginated.

For seller users: Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items and ecommerce_mall_products to find pending cancellation requests for products the seller owns. Filter where request_status = 'pending'.

Return paginated results with cursor or offset-based pagination. Sort by created_at DESC.

Include total count for pagination metadata.

Apply soft delete filter: only return records where deleted_at is NULL.

Validate user authentication before query. Return 401 if unauthenticated.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for cancellation request list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cancellation request status summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of refund requests for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint provides customers with access to their own refund requests based on their customer account. Each customer can view the status and details of all refund requests they have submitted for order items.

Supports comprehensive filtering by request status (pending, approved, rejected), creation date ranges, and pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Response includes refund request summary information optimized for list displays.

**Note**: Sellers should use the separate `/seller/refund-requests` endpoint to view refund requests for order items from products they sell.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for refund request list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summaries

operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table with pagination and filtering.

Access control:
- For customer actors: filter where orderItem.order.customer.id matches the authenticated customer ID
- For seller actors: filter where orderItem.order.customer.id can be any (seller views all requests for their order items via orderItem.product.seller relationship)

Apply filters:
- requestStatus: exact match or IN clause for multiple statuses
- createdAfter / createdBefore: date range filtering
- sortBy: supported fields are 'createdAt' and 'updatedAt'
- sortOrder: 'asc' or 'desc'

Return paginated results with cursor or offset-based pagination.
Include summary fields: id, reason (truncated if long), requestStatus, createdAt, updatedAt.

Validation:
- Verify customer/seller authentication
- Validate date format for date range filters
- Enforce page size limits (10-100 items per page)
- Ensure seller can only access order items from their own products

Edge cases:
- Return empty array if no matching requests
- Handle soft-deleted records (exclude deleted_at is null)
- Maintain audit trail via snapshot records for status changes

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive review analytics for a specific product.

This operation calculates and returns aggregated review statistics for the specified product, including the average star rating (rounded to one decimal place), total number of active reviews, and the distribution of ratings across all five star levels (5-star through 1-star).

The operation includes a preview of recent active reviews, displaying up to 10 reviews sorted by newest first. Each review preview contains the customer's display name, star rating, text content (if provided), and creation timestamp.

Only active (non-deleted) reviews are included in all calculations and listings. Products with no reviews display an average rating of null and zero review counts.

This operation is accessible to all authenticated users (customers and sellers) for browsing product information. Administrators can also access this endpoint for oversight purposes.
operations.name: getAnalytics
operations.specification:
1. Validate that product_id exists in ecommerce_mall_products table and is active (is_active=true)
2. Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table for all reviews where:
   - product_id matches the path parameter productId
   - deleted_at is NULL (active reviews only)
3. Calculate aggregate statistics:
   - average_rating: SUM(rating) / COUNT(*), rounded to 1 decimal place, or null if no reviews
   - total_count: COUNT(*) of active reviews
   - rating_distribution: GROUP BY rating with COUNT for ratings 1-5
4. Query recent reviews (limit 10):
   - ORDER BY created_at DESC
   - SELECT: id, customer.display_name, rating, text_content, created_at
5. Handle edge cases:
   - If product not found, return 404 Not Found
   - If product has no reviews, return null average_rating and empty reviews array
   - If product is inactive, return 404 Not Found
6. Join with ecommerce_mall_customers to get customer display names for review previews
7. Ensure rating calculations exclude deleted reviews from all computations

responseBody.description: Review analytics data including aggregated statistics and recent review previews

parameters.description: Product ID to retrieve review analytics for
parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete inventory history for a product variant with advanced filtering and sorting capabilities.

This endpoint provides sellers with full visibility into the stock history of any variant they own. The response displays all inventory records in reverse chronological order (newest first), showing the quantity change amount, reason for each change, and timestamp. Each record includes a running total that shows the stock balance after that transaction occurred.

Sellers can filter the history by date range to view transactions within specific time periods, and by reason type to examine specific categories of stock changes (restocking, order fulfillment, cancellation, refund, adjustment). This filtering capability supports inventory auditing and reconciliation workflows.

The endpoint is access-controlled to ensure only the variant's owning seller can view the inventory history. Customers and other actors are denied access to inventory information.

This operation is commonly used in seller dashboards and inventory management interfaces to track stock movements and investigate discrepancies.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_inventory_records table filtered by variant_id matching the path parameter.

Apply filters from request body:
- dateRange: filter records where timestamp falls within start and end dates
- reason: filter records by exact reason match (order_fulfillment, cancellation, refund, restocking, adjustment)
- sortBy: sort order (newest first by default, oldest first available)
- limit: optional limit for large result sets despite pagination-free design

operations.description:
Exports inventory history records for a product variant as a downloadable CSV file.

This operation enables sellers to download a comprehensive export of all inventory transactions for a specific variant, including quantity changes, reasons, timestamps, and cumulative stock levels. The export is useful for auditing, accounting, and inventory reconciliation purposes.

The seller must own the variant (the variant's product must belong to them) to export its inventory history. The system validates ownership before generating the export.

The exported CSV file includes all inventory records with fields: timestamp, quantity_change, reason, cumulative_stock_level, and variant_id. Records are sorted by timestamp (newest first) for chronological reference.

The export operation is read-only and does not modify any inventory records. Once the CSV file is generated, the seller can download it using the returned URI.

Related operations:
- GET /variants/{variantId} must be pre-executed to verify the variant exists and belongs to the seller before exporting.
- PATCH /variants/{variantId}/inventory/history must be used to view inventory history in the browser UI for real-time stock calculation.
operations.name: exportHistory
operations.specification:
1. Validate that variantId is a valid UUID
2. Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants to find the variant by id
3. Verify variant exists and is active (isActive = true)
4. Get the product from product_variants.product_id
5. Check that the requesting seller owns this product (product.seller_id == current_user_id)
6. If not authorized, return 403 Forbidden with error message
7. Query ecommerce_mall_inventory_records for all records where variant_id = variantId
8. Apply optional filters from query parameters:
   - startDate: filter records where timestamp >= startDate
   - endDate: filter records where timestamp <= endDate
   - reason: filter records where reason equals the specified reason (restocking, order_fulfillment, cancellation, refund, adjustment)
9. Sort results by timestamp DESC (newest first)
10. Generate CSV content with headers: timestamp,variant_id,quantity_change,reason,cumulative_stock_level
11. Calculate cumulative stock level by summing quantity_change values in chronological order (oldest to newest)
12. Generate file with UUID filename: inventory-export-{variantId}-{timestamp}.csv
13. Upload CSV to file storage service
14. Return absolute URI to the generated file as string
15. Include proper MIME type: text/csv
16. Set Content-Disposition header for file download

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: variant not found or not active
- 403 Forbidden: variant does not belong to the seller
- 400 Bad Request: invalid filter parameter format
- 500 Internal Server Error: file generation or storage failure

responseBody.description: URI string to the downloadable CSV file containing inventory history records

parameters.description: ID of the product variant to export inventory history for
parameters.name: variantId

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator grade.

This operation enables super administrators to grant elevated privileges to other administrators by changing their grade from regular to super administrator. The promoted user immediately gains all super administrator privileges including the ability to approve admin requests, promote other administrators, and access all system-wide administrative functions.

Security is strictly enforced: super administrators cannot promote themselves, and the operation will be rejected if the target user is already a super administrator or if the requesting user lacks super administrator privileges. The system validates that at least one super administrator will remain after any potential future operations.

Every promotion action creates an immutable snapshot recording the grade change, including the previous grade, new grade, performing administrator, timestamp, and reason for the change. These snapshots are preserved for audit trails, dispute resolution, and compliance tracking.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification:
Implement admin grade promotion with strict validation:

1. Authentication & Authorization:
   - Verify the requesting user is authenticated as an administrator
   - Check that the requesting user has super administrator grade
   - Reject with 403 Forbidden if user is regular administrator
   - Reject with 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated

2. Self-Promotion Prevention:
   - Compare requesting user ID with adminId path parameter
   - Reject with 409 Conflict if they match (self-promotion attempt)
   - Log the attempted self-administration action

3. Target Grade Validation:
   - Fetch the target administrator by adminId
   - Verify the target exists (404 Not Found if not)
   - Check target's current grade is 'regular' (not already super)
   - Reject with 409 Conflict if target is already super administrator
   - Verify target is not banned (is_banned = false)
   - Reject with 400 Bad Request if target account is banned

4. Grade Change Execution:
   - Begin database transaction
   - Update the target administrator's grade field to 'super'
   - Set updated_at timestamp to current time
   - Commit transaction

5. Snapshot Creation:
   - Create immutable ecommerce_mall_admin_request_snapshots record
   - Record fields: id (UUID), ecommerce_mall_admin_request_request_id (null for promotions), changed_by (requesting admin's ID), reason ('Admin promoted to super administrator by {performing_admin}'), request_status ('approved'), created_at (original created_at from target admin), changed_at (current timestamp)
   - This snapshot preserves the grade change for audit purposes

6. Notification:
   - Generate system notification to the promoted user
   - Document new privileges granted
   - Log the promotion event in admin activity logs

7. Response:
   - Return updated administrator record with new super grade
   - Include grade, updated_at, and all current admin fields

Error Codes:
- 401: Unauthorized - user not authenticated
- 403: Forbidden - user is regular administrator, not super
- 404: Not Found - target administrator does not exist
- 409: Conflict - self-promotion attempt or target already super
- 400: Bad Request - target account is banned

responseBody.description: Updated administrator with super administrator grade after successful promotion

parameters.name: adminId
parameters.description: UUID of the administrator to be promoted to super administrator

requestBody.description: Promotion metadata including reason and performing administrator context

operations.description:
Review a pending administrator access request by approving or rejecting it.

This operation allows a super administrator to review a specific admin request and make a decision to either approve or reject the request. When approved, the requesting user (customer or seller) is granted regular administrator privileges. When rejected, the request is marked as rejected and the user may submit a new request.

The requesting user's identity and current role (customer or seller) must be verified before granting admin privileges. The operation requires a valid admin request ID and the reviewer's super administrator credentials to ensure only authorized personnel can modify request statuses.

The operation creates an immutable snapshot of the status change for audit purposes, recording the previous status, new status, performing super administrator, and timestamp of the change.
operations.name: review
operations.specification:
1. Validate the admin request exists and is in 'pending' status
2. Verify the requesting user has a pending request with the given ID
3. Load the admin request record with associated requester information
4. Validate the current user is a super administrator
5. Process the approval or rejection decision:
   - If approved: Update request status to 'approved', grant admin role to requester, create admin record if needed
   - If rejected: Update request status to 'rejected'
6. Create an immutable snapshot recording the status change with oldValues, newValues, changedBy, changedAt
7. Notify the requesting user of the status change
8. Return the updated admin request record with new status

Database operations:
- SELECT FROM ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests WHERE id = {requestId} AND request_status = 'pending'
- UPDATE ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests SET request_status = '{status}', updated_at = NOW()
- INSERT INTO ecommerce_mall_admin_request_snapshots (recordType, recordId, changes, oldValues, newValues, changedBy, changedAt)
- INSERT INTO ecommerce_mall_admins (if approved and no existing admin record)

responseBody.description: The updated admin request record with the new status after review

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the admin request to review

operations.specification:
Query multiple database tables to compute aggregated metrics for the observability dashboard:
1. Order lifecycle: Count orders from ecommerce_mall_orders by overallStatus (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) for current period
2. Seller approval queue: Count pending requests from ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests, calculate average wait time (days since createdAt for pending), fetch oldest 10 pending requests
3. Inventory alerts: Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants where stockQuantity < 10 to identify variants in warning state
4. Review analytics: Count total reviews from ecommerce_mall_reviews, calculate average rating, count reviews with isActive=false (pending moderation), count reviews that might match spam patterns
5. System status: Check if system is operational based on API health, database connection pool utilization, and payment processing success rate metrics
6. Seller metrics: Count total products from ecommerce_mall_products, count order items from ecommerce_mall_order_items
7. Audit log metrics: Count total audit entries from ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs

Return aggregated metrics in IObservabilityDashboard.ISummary structure. All metrics should be computed fresh from database queries (not from cached/pre-computed tables) as per real-time dashboard requirements with maximum 1-minute refresh interval.

Permissions: This endpoint is accessible to admins (as per section 1310 - 'administrators, system operators, and assigned support personnel').
operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive system-wide observability metrics and statistics for monitoring ecommerce platform health and performance.

This dashboard provides real-time insights into order lifecycle tracking, review analytics, inventory status, seller approval queues, and system operational state. The metrics are aggregated from multiple database entities including orders, reviews, product variants, seller profiles, and audit logs to give a complete picture of platform performance.

**Data Sources**:
- Database metrics: Computed fresh from ecommerce_mall_orders, ecommerce_mall_reviews, ecommerce_mall_product_variants, ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests, ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs tables
- Infrastructure metrics: Retrieved from external monitoring systems (API latency, connection pool usage, cache performance)

**Dashboard Features**:
- Real-time order statistics with status breakdowns (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)
- Seller approval queue with wait time analytics
- Inventory alert system for low-stock variants (below 10 units threshold)
- Review analytics including moderation queue counts
- System health indicators with automated status determination

**Access Control**:
This endpoint is accessible to administrators and authorized support personnel only. Regular customers and sellers cannot access system-wide observability metrics. Access is enforced via role-based authorization checks at the service layer.

All metrics are updated with maximum 1-minute refresh interval as per observability dashboard requirements. The dashboard supports custom time range selection and can export current state as screenshots or PDF reports for administrative reporting.

responseBody.description: Aggregated observability metrics including order lifecycle, review analytics, inventory alerts, seller approval queue, and system status indicators.

IEcommerceMallSeller.description:
Complete seller account entity representing a merchant on the ecommerce platform.

This type captures the full seller account information including authentication metadata (email address), approval status (pending, approved, or rejected), rejection reason if the application was declined, and account state flags for suspension and banning. The seller account is the foundation for all selling activities including product listings, order fulfillment, and customer interactions.

The approval_status field determines seller capability: 'pending' means awaiting administrator review, 'approved' allows selling activities, and 'rejected' prevents selling until resubmission. The is_suspended flag indicates temporary loss of privileges, while is_banned marks permanent platform exclusion.

Related operations: View own account (GET), update profile (PATCH), administrators can list/filter (PATCH), permanently delete (DELETE).

Retrieve: id (UUID), email, approval_status, rejection_reason (if applicable), is_suspended, is_banned, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Excluded: password_hash (security). Authorization: authenticated seller can view own account, admin can view any seller.

IEcommerceMallProduct.IRequest.description: Request parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating product list queries.
IEcommerceMallProduct.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating product list queries. These parameters are used as query parameters in the GET /ecommerceMall/products endpoint to build WHERE clauses, ORDER BY, and LIMIT/OFFSET for the product listing query. The query joins ecommerce_mall_products with ecommerce_mall_categories (for category filtering and name display), ecommerce_mall_sellers (for seller filtering and shop_name display), and ecommerce_mall_product_images (for image count sorting). Filters: category_id (exact match), seller_id (exact match, verified against auth user for non-admins), is_active (boolean flag), name_search (partial match via LIKE or full-text search on name column), created_after (created_at >= value), created_before (created_at <= value), min_price (base_price >= value), max_price (base_price <= value). Sorting: sort_by (one of: created_at, base_price, name, image_count), sort_direction (asc or desc). Pagination: page (1-indexed, default 1), limit (1-100, default 20). Authorization: customers see only is_active=true products by default; sellers see all their own products; admins see all products.

Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and retrieving category listings.

Provides flexible query capabilities for administrators to search and filter the product category catalog. Supports partial text matching (case-insensitive) on category names and descriptions, hierarchical filtering by parent category, soft-deletion filtering, combined full-text search, and customizable sorting and pagination. IEcommerceMallProduct.description:
Complete product entity with all public fields, nested seller and category profiles, product variants, images, audit snapshots, and review information.

This schema represents a single product in the ecommerce catalog, including denormalized seller shop profile data for efficient display. The seller information contains shop branding details (shop name, description, logo) retrieved from the seller profiles table. Category information includes the full category name and hierarchical parent chain for product navigation breadcrumbs.

Product variants are included as a nested array, showing all available option combinations (e.g., size, color) with their SKU codes, option values, and pricing overrides. Images are returned in display order, with the first image serving as the main product thumbnail.

Audit snapshots preserve historical state changes for dispute resolution. Review aggregates provide customer feedback with ratings and text content.

Products returned by this endpoint must be active (is_active=true), not soft-deleted, and owned by sellers who are not suspended from the platform.
IEcommerceMallProduct.x-autobe-specification:
Direct fields: id, name, description, base_price, is_active, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at from ecommerce_mall_products table.

Relations via JOIN:
- seller: JOIN ecommerce_mall_sellers ON seller_id, then JOIN ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles ON seller_id to get shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url. Filter: seller.is_suspended=false, seller.deleted_at is null.
- category: JOIN ecommerce_mall_categories ON category_id. Get name and parent category chain for breadcrumbs.

Compositions:
- variants: JOIN ecommerce_mall_product_variants ON product_id with is_active filter. Return full variant details with option_values JSON.
- images: JOIN ecommerce_mall_product_images ON product_id ORDER BY display_order ASC. First image is main product thumbnail.
- snapshots: JOIN ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots ON record_id=product.id AND record_type='ecommerce_mall_products'. Return immutable audit trail.
- reviews: JOIN ecommerce_mall_reviews ON product_id WHERE is_active=true. Return review details with rating and text_content.

Aggregations:
- wishlist_entries_count: COUNT(wishlist.product_id WHERE product.id = wishlist.product_id)
- order_items_count: COUNT(order_item.product_id WHERE product.id = order_item.product_id)
- reviews_count: COUNT(reviews.product_id WHERE product.id = product.id AND reviews.is_active=true)

Filter criteria:
- product.is_active=true
- product.deleted_at is null
- seller.is_suspended=false
- seller.deleted_at is null
- category.deleted_at is null

Return 404 if product not found, not active, or owned by suspended seller.

The system validates that this variant belongs to the product referenced in the wishlist entry (variant.product_id must equal wishlist_entry.product_id), that the variant is active (is_active = true), and that it has available stock (stock_quantity > 0). If validation passes, a cart item is created or updated with quantity=1 and price captured at addition time.

IEcommerceMallWishlistToCartRequest.description: Request body for transferring a product from your wishlist to your shopping cart. This operation enables you to quickly add a wishlisted product to your cart by selecting a specific variant. Since wishlists store products (not variants) while shopping carts require specific variant selections, you must provide both the wishlist entry identifier and the variant ID to add. The system will validate that the variant belongs to the wishlisted product and has available stock before adding it to your cart.
IEcommerceMallWishlistToCartRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request body for transferring a product from customer wishlist to shopping cart. The operation receives wishlistEntryId (UUID referencing a wishlist entry in ecommerce_mall_wishlists table) and variantId (UUID referencing a product variant in ecommerce_mall_product_variants table). The system validates that the variant belongs to the wishlisted product, is active, and has available stock. If a cart item already exists for this variant in the customer's active cart, the quantity is incremented; otherwise, a new cart item is created with quantity=1 and price captured from the variant. The wishlist entry remains unchanged as carts and wishlists maintain independent states. This is a composed request that triggers multiple database operations (wishlist validation via ecommerce_mall_wishlists, variant lookup via ecommerce_mall_product_variants, cart management, cart item creation/update).

IEcommerceMallCategorySnapshot.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating category snapshot records.

This type defines the search criteria and pagination options for retrieving historical category snapshot records. Categories are organized hierarchically with parent-child relationships, and this request allows administrators to filter snapshots by category reference, name patterns, date ranges, and leaf status.

The request supports flexible date range filtering on multiple timestamp fields (snapshot creation time, original category creation time, last update time) to enable audit trail exploration. Pagination uses cursor-style with configurable page sizes and sorting options.
IEcommerceMallCategorySnapshot.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Filter and paginate category snapshots from ecommerce_mall_category_snapshots table.

Filters:
- ecommerce_mall_category_id: UUID filter on referenced category ID
- name: Partial match on category name at snapshot time
- snapshot_created_at_from/to: Filter by snapshot creation timestamp range
- created_at_from/to: Filter by original category creation timestamp range
- updated_at_from/to: Filter by original category update timestamp range
- is_leaf: Filter by leaf category status (boolean)

Pagination:
- page: Integer >= 1 (1-indexed page number)
- limit: Integer 1-100 (records per page)
- sort: Field name for sorting (snapshot_created_at, name, created_at, updated_at, is_leaf, id)
- order: asc/desc (default: desc)

Note: This is a query filter type, not a direct table mapping. databaseSchema=null.

Records are ordered by timestamp descending (newest first). The running_total field in each item is calculated by the server as cumulative sum of quantity_change from earliest to current record, providing running balance history.

IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.IHistoryLi.description: Complete inventory history list with running stock totals. This response type contains all inventory change records for a product variant, displaying the chronological history of stock movements along with calculated running totals that show the stock balance after each transaction. Records are ordered by timestamp in descending order (newest first). The running_total field provides visibility into stock levels at each point in history, enabling sellers to audit stock movements and track balance changes over time.
IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.IHistoryLi.x-autobe-specification: Response object containing: records array of inventory history items. Each record maps to ecommerce_mall_inventory_records with: id (primary key), variant_id (FK), quantity_change (int), reason (string enum: order_fulfillment, cancellation, refund, restocking, adjustment), timestamp (date-time), running_total (calculated: cumulative sum of quantity_change from earliest record to current). Query source: ecommerce_mall_inventory_records filtered by variant_id. Running total calculated by server by summing all quantity_change values chronologically from first to current record. Filter by dateRange and reason applied in query. Sort by timestamp descending (newest first).

data.x-autobe-specification: Computed order lifecycle metrics aggregated from ecommerce_mall_orders table. Each field counts orders by their overall_status: ordersCreated (paid), ordersShipped (shipped), ordersDelivered (delivered), ordersCancelled (cancelled), ordersRefunded (refunded), totalOrders (all statuses). Values are calculated using SQL aggregate functions with optional filtering by date range and status.

IEcommerceMallOrderAnalytic.ISummary.description: Aggregated order lifecycle analytics metrics with pagination metadata. This response type provides a summary of orders distributed across different lifecycle stages (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) for efficient dashboard display and reporting. Contains count metrics per status and pagination information for large result sets.
IEcommerceMallOrderAnalytic.ISummary.x-autobe-specification:
Compute order lifecycle analytics metrics from ecommerce_mall_orders table using SQL aggregate functions.

Aggregation logic:
- ordersCreated: COUNT(*) WHERE overall_status = 'paid'
- ordersShipped: COUNT(*) WHERE overall_status = 'shipped'
- ordersDelivered: COUNT(*) WHERE overall_status = 'delivered'
- ordersCancelled: COUNT(*) WHERE overall_status = 'cancelled'
- ordersRefunded: COUNT(*) WHERE overall_status = 'refunded'
- totalOrders: COUNT(*) for all filtered records

Query must:
1. Apply optional filters from IEcommerceMallOrderAnalytic.IRequest: fromDate (created_at >=), toDate (created_at <=), overall_status
2. Use SQL aggregate functions (COUNT with CASE WHEN or GROUP BY overall_status)
3. Calculate pagination metadata: totalPages = ceil(totalItems / pageSize)
4. Handle edge cases: empty result sets (all counts = 0)

Return response structure:
{
  pagination: { page, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages },
  data: { ordersCreated, ordersShipped, ordersDelivered, ordersCancelled, ordersRefunded, totalOrders }
}

No JOINs required as all aggregation is from ecommerce_mall_orders table. Use efficient indexing on (created_at, overall_status) for optimal query performance.

Returns null when no reviews exist (division by zero handled). Range: 0.0 to 5.0 based on valid rating values in reviews table.

total_count.description: The total number of active (non-deleted) reviews for this product.
total_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed value: COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_reviews where product_id matches and deleted_at IS NULL. Returns integer >= 0. Counts only active reviews, excluding soft-deleted records.

rating_distribution.x-autobe-specification: Computed object with 5 keys (rating5_count, rating4_count, rating3_count, rating2_count, rating1_count). Each key holds COUNT(*) of reviews from ecommerce_mall_reviews where product_id matches, deleted_at IS NULL, and rating equals the key number. All counts are >= 0 and sum to total_count.

recent_reviews.description: Up to 10 most recent review previews for this product, sorted by creation date (newest first). Each review includes the customer's display name, star rating, optional text content, and creation timestamp.
recent_reviews.x-autobe-specification: Computed array with max 10 items. SELECT id, customer.display_name, rating, text_content, created_at FROM ecommerce_mall_reviews INNER JOIN ecommerce_mall_customers ON reviews.customer_id=customers.id WHERE reviews.product_id=:productId AND reviews.deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY reviews.created_at DESC LIMIT 10. Each item represents one active review with customer display name, rating, optional text, and creation timestamp.

IReviewAnalyticsResponse.description: Review analytics response containing aggregated statistics for a product's reviews. Includes the average star rating (0-5, rounded to 1 decimal), total count of active reviews, breakdown of ratings across all 5 star levels, and a preview of up to 10 most recent reviews with customer information. Only active (non-deleted) reviews are included in all calculations.
IReviewAnalyticsResponse.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation response that does not map to a single database table. Aggregation logic: (1) average_rating = SUM(rating)/COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_reviews WHERE product_id=:productId AND deleted_at IS NULL, rounded to 1 decimal place, or null if no reviews exist. (2) total_count = COUNT(*) of active reviews (deleted_at IS NULL). (3) rating_distribution = GROUP BY rating with COUNT(*) for ratings 1-5, returning keys: rating5_count, rating4_count, rating3_count, rating2_count, rating1_count. (4) recent_reviews = SELECT id, customer.display_name, rating, text_content, created_at FROM ecommerce_mall_reviews INNER JOIN ecommerce_mall_customers ON reviews.customer_id=customers.id WHERE reviews.product_id=:productId AND reviews.deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY reviews.created_at DESC LIMIT 10. Edge cases: null average_rating when no reviews, empty reviews array, all distribution counts=0.

IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboard.description: Aggregated dashboard metrics and system status indicators for administrative monitoring and observability. This schema represents a comprehensive view of system health, business operations, and user activity across the ecommerce platform. It provides administrators with real-time insights into order processing, product inventory, seller approvals, customer reviews, and system performance. The dashboard aggregates data from multiple source tables and computes key performance indicators including error rates, order status distributions, inventory levels, approval queue metrics, and user activity trends. Time-series data is included to enable trend analysis and chart visualization in administrative interfaces.
IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Compute from multiple sources:

1. systemStatus: Derived from error_rate (green < 1%, yellow < 5%, red >= 5%)
2. systemHealth: Query ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs, count errors by action_type, calculate error_rate over 5-min windows
3. orderLifecycle: Query ecommerce_mall_orders, count by overall_status (created/shipped/delivered/cancelled/refunded), join with order_items for item metrics
4. reviewAnalytics: Query ecommerce_mall_reviews, calculate average rating, count by star distribution (1-5), track pending moderation counts
5. inventoryHealth: Query ecommerce_mall_inventory_records + product_variants, count variants with stock_quantity < 10 (below threshold per section 1310)
6. sellerApprovalQueue: Query ecommerce_mall_sellers where approval_status = 'pending', count total, calculate average wait time, retrieve oldest 5 entries (paginated)
7. userActivity: Count active users from ecommerce_mall_customers, ecommerce_mall_sellers, ecommerce_mall_admins; count active sessions from *_sessions tables; compute concurrent_users from session overlap

Time series data: Generate {timestamp, value} arrays with granularity based on time range (hourly <24h, daily 24h-30d, weekly >30d)

Edge cases: Return zero counts if no data exists, partial dashboard if computation exceeds 10s, all timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC

Default: 10. Enforced by service layer validation.

If provided, cannot also use custom start_date/end_date. Time series data granularity is computed from this range: hourly for <24h, daily for 24h-30d, weekly for >30d.

Null = no service filtering (aggregate all services). Used primarily for systemHealth metrics including error_rate calculations and critical alert detection.

Service layer filters metrics by user type: 'customer' (from ecommerce_mall_customers), 'seller' (from ecommerce_mall_sellers), 'admin' (from ecommerce_mall_admins). Null = aggregate all user types. Applies to orderLifecycle metrics (customer orders), sellerApprovalQueue metrics (seller approvals), and userActivity metrics (session counts).

IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboard.IRe.description: Query parameters for filtering and configuring the observability dashboard metrics aggregation. Allows administrators to specify time ranges, actor types, service components, geographic regions, and pagination for detailed views. All parameters are optional - unspecified filters return data across all dimensions. Used exclusively for the admin observability dashboard endpoint to enable targeted investigation of system behavior.
IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboard.IRe.x-autobe-specification:
Request body for observability dashboard filtering and time range configuration. Not a database table - this is a parameter DTO that specifies aggregation criteria for the service layer to compute metrics from multiple tables (ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs, ecommerce_mall_orders, ecommerce_mall_reviews, ecommerce_mall_product_variants, ecommerce_mall_inventory_records, ecommerce_mall_sellers, session tables).

Parameters (all optional):
1. predefined_time_range: Predefined time window (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, 180d, 365d). Service computes startDate and endDate from this value.
2. user_type: Filter metrics by actor type (customer, seller, admin). Null = aggregate all types.
3. service: Filter system health metrics by service component. Null = all services.
4. region: Filter by geographic region from session metadata. Null = all regions.
5. page, limit: Pagination parameters for seller approval queue list only (1-based page, 1-100 limit).

Validation (service layer): If predefined_time_range is provided, cannot also use start_date/end_date. Date range must not exceed 365 days. Page must be >= 1. Limit must be 1-100.

Computation logic: Parse predefined_time_range to compute time window. Query multiple tables with filters applied. Generate time-series data with appropriate granularity (hourly <24h, daily 24h-30d, weekly >30d). Apply filters to each metric type as appropriate. Paginate seller approval queue if pagination params provided. Return filter_context documenting applied filters for reproducibility.

Computation logic:
1. page = request.page parameter (default: 1, validated >= 1)
2. limit = request.limit parameter (default: 10, validated 1-100 per business rules)
3. totalItems = COUNT(*) from database query matching filters
4. totalPages = CEIL(totalItems / limit)

Data flow:
- page, limit: extracted from request parameters (IPage.IRequest)
- totalItems: server-side COUNT(*) query on source table with applied filters
- totalPages: server-side calculation (totalItems / limit, rounded up)

- totalItems=0 → totalPages=0
- Invalid page parameter → reject with 400 error
- limit > 100 → cap at 100 per business rules

IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboard.IFi.x-autobe-specification:
FilterContext captures the filter parameters applied when querying the observability dashboard. All filters are passed from IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboard.IRequest and stored in the response for transparency and reproducibility. Computation logic:

1. userType: Accept 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', or null (aggregate all). If null, dashboard metrics are computed across all actor types. If set, metrics are filtered by the specified actor type.

Provides administrators with a quick overview of the seller approval backlog, including the total number of pending applications awaiting review, the average time sellers wait for approval, and a list of the oldest pending requests to prioritize.
IEcommerceMallSellerApprovalQueue.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregated seller approval queue metrics computed from ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests JOINed with ecommerce_mall_admin_request_request_of_sellers.

1. totalPendingCount: COUNT(*) of admin requests where request_status = 'pending' AND the requester is a seller (via ecommerce_mall_admin_request_request_of_sellers JOIN). Soft-delete excluded (deleted_at IS NULL).
2. averageWaitTime: AVG(DATEDIFF(NOW(), created_at)) in days for pending seller requests. Returns null when totalPendingCount = 0.
3. oldestPendingRequests: SELECT id, reason, request_status, created_at, updated_at FROM ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests INNER JOIN ecommerce_mall_admin_request_request_of_sellers ON requests.id = seller_requests.request_id WHERE requests.deleted_at IS NULL AND requests.request_status = 'pending' ORDER BY requests.created_at ASC LIMIT 10. Returns IEcommerceMallAdminRequestRequest.ISummary for each request.

Query pattern: SELECT COUNT(*) as total, AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(DAY, created_at, NOW())) as avg_wait FROM ecommerce_mall_admin_request_requests r INNER JOIN ecommerce_mall_admin_request_request_of_sellers s ON r.id = s.request_id WHERE r.deleted_at IS NULL AND r.request_status = 'pending'.

Edge cases: If no pending seller requests exist, totalPendingCount=0, averageWaitTime=null, oldestPendingRequests=[]. All timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC format.

IEcommerceMallUserActivityMetric.description: Aggregated user activity metrics for the admin observability dashboard. Provides real-time monitoring of platform activity including active user counts by type (customers, sellers, administrators), active session counts for each user type, total active sessions across all user types, and concurrent users representing unique users with active sessions during the dashboard time window.
IEcommerceMallUserActivityMetric.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from multiple tables for admin observability dashboard:

1. Active user counts (all-time, excluding soft-deleted):
   - activeCustomers: COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM ecommerce_mall_customers WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
   - activeSellers: COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM ecommerce_mall_sellers WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
   - activeAdmins: COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM ecommerce_mall_admins WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

2. Active session counts (within dashboard time window):
   - customerSessionCount: COUNT(id) FROM ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions WHERE expires_at >= dashboard_end_time
   - sellerSessionCount: COUNT(id) FROM ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions WHERE expires_at >= dashboard_end_time
   - adminSessionCount: COUNT(id) FROM ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions WHERE expires_at >= dashboard_end_time

3. Aggregated metrics:
   - totalActiveSessions: SUM(customerSessionCount + sellerSessionCount + adminSessionCount)
   - concurrentUsers: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id, session_type) from all session tables where expires_at >= dashboard_end_time
   - Represents unique users with active sessions at any point during the dashboard time window

Edge cases: Return 0 for all counts if no data exists in time window. All values are >= 0.

IDateRange.description:
Date range filter for querying time-series data by timestamp boundaries.

Used for filtering records created within a specific time period. Both start_date and end_date are optional, allowing flexible query patterns such as "all records after date X", "all records before date Y", or "all records between dates X and Y". The datetime values must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
IDateRange.x-autobe-specification:
Date range filter for querying time-series data by timestamp boundaries.

Usage: IEcommerceMallAdminAuditLog.IRequest.date_range parameter.

Implementation:
- start_date (optional): ISO 8601 datetime string, filters records where created_at >= start_date
- end_date (optional): ISO 8601 datetime string, filters records where created_at <= end_date
- Both fields are optional (at least one may be provided)
- When both provided: WHERE created_at >= start_date AND created_at <= end_date
- When only start_date provided: WHERE created_at >= start_date
- When only end_date provided: WHERE created_at <= end_date
- Use PostgreSQL timestamptz type for datetime comparisons
- Validate ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sss+HH:MM
- Edge cases: start_date after end_date should be handled (either reject with 400 or swap)

isOperational.description: Overall system operational status indicating if all critical metrics are within acceptable thresholds.
isOperational.x-autobe-specification: Computed boolean - true if apiHealth='healthy' AND databaseConnectionPoolUtilization < 0.9 AND paymentProcessingSuccessRate > 0.95, false otherwise

IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboardSumm.description: System operational status metrics computed from external monitoring services. Provides a comprehensive view of platform health including API status, database pool utilization, payment success rate, cache performance, and overall operational state.
IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboardSumm.x-autobe-specification: Computed from external monitoring APIs: apiHealth (health endpoint), apiLatencyMs (API response time), databaseConnectionPoolUtilization (DB pool percentage), paymentProcessingSuccessRate (payment gateway monitoring), cacheHitRate (cache monitoring), errorRate (application monitoring), activeConnections (server monitoring), isOperational (computed boolean from critical thresholds)

paid_count.description: Number of orders currently in paid status.
paid_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE overallStatus = 'paid'. Count of all orders with paid status. Integer >= 0. Updated in real-time as orders transition through their lifecycle.

shipped_count.description: Number of orders currently in shipped status.
shipped_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE overallStatus = 'shipped'. Count of all orders that have been shipped but not yet delivered. Integer >= 0. Updated in real-time as orders transition through their lifecycle.

delivered_count.description: Number of orders currently in delivered status.
delivered_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE overallStatus = 'delivered'. Count of all orders that have been delivered to customers. Integer >= 0. Updated in real-time as orders transition through their lifecycle.

cancelled_count.description: Number of orders currently in cancelled status.
cancelled_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE overallStatus = 'cancelled'. Count of all orders that have been cancelled. Integer >= 0. Updated in real-time as orders transition through their lifecycle.

refunded_count.description: Number of orders currently in refunded status.
refunded_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE overallStatus = 'refunded'. Count of all orders that have been refunded. Integer >= 0. Updated in real-time as orders transition through their lifecycle.

IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboardSumm.description: Aggregated breakdown of order counts by their current status. Provides real-time visibility into the distribution of orders across the 5 lifecycle states (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded). Used in the admin observability dashboard for monitoring platform order health.
IEcommerceMallObservabilityDashboardSumm.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from ecommerce_mall_orders table. Queries SELECT overallStatus, COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_orders GROUP BY overallStatus. Returns 5 count fields corresponding to the 5 possible status values: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded. Each field stores the count of orders with that status. Computed fresh for each dashboard query (no caching). Used in observability dashboard for real-time order lifecycle visibility.

error_counts.description: Error counts grouped by action type. Each key represents an action type from audit logs, and the value is the count of errors (status = 'error' or 'failure') for that action within the time window.
error_counts.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs: GROUP BY action_type, COUNT(*) where status IN ('error', 'failure'). Returns an object keyed by action_type with integer counts. Example: {"order-create": 5, "payment-process": 2}. All action_types from audit logs within time window are included, even if count is 0.

error_rate.description: Error rate percentage calculated over the last 5-minute window. Computed as (error_count / total_count) * 100. Returns null if no audit log entries exist. Range: 0.0 (no errors) to 100.0 (all errors).
error_rate.x-autobe-specification: Computed from error_count / total_count * 100. Divides time window into 5-minute segments per section 1282. Returns null if no audit log entries exist. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Thresholds: < 1% = green (healthy), 1-5% = yellow (degraded), >= 5% = red (critical).

total_count.description: Total number of audit log entries within the time window, regardless of status. Used as the denominator for error_rate calculation.
total_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs within the time window, regardless of status. Used as the denominator for error_rate calculation. Returns 0 if no entries exist.

error_count.description: Total number of error/failure audit log entries within the time window. Used as the numerator for error_rate calculation.
error_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs where status IN ('error', 'failure') within the time window. Used as the numerator for error_rate calculation. Returns 0 if no errors exist.

critical_alerts.description: List of critical alerts triggered when error rates exceed thresholds. Empty if all metrics are within acceptable ranges. Sorted by severity (highest first).
critical_alerts.x-autobe-specification: Computed from error_rate thresholds: if error_rate > 1% flag as yellow/degraded, if > 5% flag as red/critical. Array of alert objects with type, action_type, current_rate, threshold, severity. Empty if all metrics within acceptable ranges. Sorted by severity (highest first).

last_error_timestamps.description: Most recent error timestamps grouped by action type. Useful for debugging recent issues. Contains ISO 8601 UTC timestamps. Null values indicate no recent errors for that action type.
last_error_timestamps.x-autobe-specification: Computed MAX(created_at) grouped by action_type for each action_type that has errors. Returns ISO 8601 UTC timestamps. Null values for action_types without recent errors. Useful for debugging and identifying most recent issues per action type.

IEcommerceMallSystemHealthMetric.description: Aggregated system health metrics computed from administrative audit logs. Provides real-time insights into system error patterns including error counts by action type, calculated error rates over 5-minute windows, and identification of critical alerts when error rates exceed defined thresholds. Enables administrators to monitor system health, detect performance degradation, and identify problematic operations requiring attention.
IEcommerceMallSystemHealthMetric.x-autobe-specification:
Computed system health metrics aggregation from ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs:

1. error_counts: GROUP BY action_type, COUNT(*) where status IN ('error', 'failure')
2. error_rate: (error_count / total_count) * 100, computed per 5-minute window
3. total_count: COUNT(*) from audit_logs in time window (all statuses)
4. error_count: COUNT(*) where status IN ('error', 'failure') in time window
5. critical_alerts: Derived thresholds - error_rate > 1% (yellow/degraded), > 5% (red/critical)
6. last_error_timestamps: MAX(created_at) grouped by action_type for each action with errors

All metrics computed with time-window filtering and timezone-normalized to UTC ISO 8601.

quantity.description: Number of units of this product variant purchased.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.quantity. Integer >= 1. Represents number of units of this variant purchased. Quantities are combined if same variant added multiple times to cart before checkout (section 183).

unit_price.description: Price per unit at the time of purchase.
unit_price.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.unit_price. Decimal number representing price per unit at purchase time. Immutable snapshot preserved even if variant price changes later. Total price computed as unit_price × quantity.

product_id.description: UUID reference to the purchased product.
product_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.ecommerce_mall_product_id. UUID reference to the parent product entity. Used to join and verify product exists, though full product data is preserved in product_snapshot for historical accuracy.

variant_id.description: UUID reference to the purchased product variant.
variant_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id. UUID reference to the specific product variant (option combination) purchased. Used to verify variant exists and track inventory, though variant data preserved in snapshot for order history.

product_snapshot.description: Immutable product data snapshot at time of purchase as JSON string.
product_snapshot.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.product_snapshot. JSON string containing immutable product data snapshot at time of purchase. Computed by fetching product entity (id, name, description, category, base_price, images) and serializing to JSON at order creation time. Preserved even if original product is deleted or modified (section 186, 562).

variant_snapshot.description: Immutable variant data snapshot at time of purchase as JSON string.
variant_snapshot.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.variant_snapshot. JSON string containing immutable variant data snapshot at time of purchase. Computed by fetching variant entity (sku_code, option_values, price_override, stock_quantity) and serializing to JSON at order creation time. Preserved even if variant is deleted or modified (section 186).

seller_profile_snapshot.description: Immutable seller profile snapshot at time of purchase as JSON string.
seller_profile_snapshot.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.seller_profile_snapshot. JSON string containing immutable seller profile snapshot at time of purchase. Computed by fetching seller profile (shop_name, logo, shop_description) and serializing to JSON at order creation time. Preserved even if seller profile is modified (section 186).

IEcommerceMallOrderItem.ICreate.description: Request body for creating an order item during checkout. Captures product variant selection, purchase quantity, and preserves immutable snapshots of product, variant, and seller profile data at purchase time for order history and dispute resolution.
IEcommerceMallOrderItem.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Creates order item at checkout. Direct mappings: quantity (integer >=1), unit_price (decimal number), product_id (UUID from ecommerce_mall_product_id column), variant_id (UUID from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id column). Snapshot columns: product_snapshot, variant_snapshot, seller_profile_snapshot (JSON strings from ecommerce_mall_order_items). FK resolution: parent order_id resolved from parent Order context, not user-provided. Business logic: persist quantity and unit_price, persist snapshot JSON strings, link to order via parent relationship.

IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.description: Shopping cart management operation. Represents a single cart manipulation action that can be executed as part of a batch operation. Supports adding product variants to cart, updating quantities, removing items, and synchronizing cart state. Each operation targets a ProductVariant by UUID and is executed within an ACID transaction to ensure data consistency.
IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.x-autobe-specification:
Cart management operation union type. NOT a database table mapping. This is a computation DTO representing different operation types executed sequentially within an ACID transaction. The type is a oneOf union of four named operation schemas:

1. IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperationAdd - Add variant to cart
2. IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperationUpdateQuantity - Update item quantity
3. IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperationRemove - Remove item from cart
4. IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperationSync - Sync cart state

Each operation targets a ProductVariant by UUID and is executed within an ACID transaction.

order_count.description: Total number of orders in the time window, excluding soft-deleted orders.
order_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregate: COUNT(DISTINCT order.id) from ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE deleted_at IS NULL within the specified time window. Excludes soft-deleted orders to reflect active business transactions.

paid_count.description: Number of orders with paid status.

shipped_count.description: Number of orders with shipped status.

delivered_count.description: Number of orders with delivered status.

cancelled_count.description: Number of orders with cancelled status.

refunded_count.description: Number of orders with refunded status.

partially_completed_count.description: Number of orders with partiallyCompleted status.

status_distribution.description: Breakdown of order count by overall_status, showing how many orders are in each fulfillment state (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partiallyCompleted).
status_distribution.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregate: COUNT(orders) GROUP BY overall_status from ecommerce_mall_orders WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Returns breakdown with fields: paid_count, shipped_count, delivered_count, cancelled_count, refunded_count, partially_completed_count. Each count represents orders with that specific status.

total_items.description: Total number of items across all orders.

item_metrics.description: Breakdown of item quantities by item_status, showing total items and quantities in each fulfillment state (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded).
item_metrics.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregate: SUM(order_items.quantity) GROUP BY item_status from ecommerce_mall_order_items. Returns: total_items (sum of all quantities), paid_items, shipped_items, delivered_items, cancelled_items, refunded_items (sum of quantities per status). Reflects fulfillment progress at the item level rather than order level.

total_revenue.description: Total revenue from all orders (sum of total_price).

average_order_value.description: Average order value calculated as total_revenue / order_count.

price_metrics.description: Revenue metrics calculated from order totals: total_revenue (sum of all order prices) and average_order_value (revenue divided by order count).
price_metrics.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregate from ecommerce_mall_orders: total_revenue = SUM(orders.total_price) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL; average_order_value = total_revenue / order_count. Both values calculated over the specified time window. Currency values should be normalized to a single currency (e.g., USD) for aggregation.

order_count_delta.description: Change in order count compared to previous period (positive = increase, negative = decrease).

revenue_delta.description: Change in total revenue compared to previous period (positive = increase, negative = decrease).

paid_to_shipped.description: Count of orders that transitioned from paid to shipped.

shipped_to_delivered.description: Count of orders that transitioned from shipped to delivered.

delivered_to_refunded.description: Count of orders that transitioned from delivered to refunded.

cancelled_count.description: Count of orders that were cancelled in this period.

status_change_breakdown.description: Count of order status transitions during the period.

period_comparison.description: Comparison metrics between current and previous time period, including changes in order count and revenue, plus a breakdown of status transitions (orders that moved between states during the period).
period_comparison.x-autobe-specification: Computed comparison between current time window and previous same-duration window: order_count_delta = current_order_count - previous_order_count; revenue_delta = current_total_revenue - previous_total_revenue. status_change_breakdown counts orders that transitioned between statuses during the period: paid_to_shipped (orders moving from paid to shipped), shipped_to_delivered (orders moving from shipped to delivered), delivered_to_refunded (orders moving from delivered to refunded), cancelled_count (orders cancelled in this period).

snapshot_at.description: Timestamp when this metrics snapshot was captured, in ISO 8601 UTC format.
snapshot_at.x-autobe-specification: Computed timestamp: Current server timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format (e.g., 2026-03-10T11:29:16.610Z) when this metrics snapshot was captured and returned to the API consumer. Used to indicate data freshness and enable caching strategies.

IEcommerceMallOrderLifecycleMetric.description: Aggregated order lifecycle metrics for administrative monitoring and business intelligence. This schema provides a comprehensive snapshot of order processing health, including order counts by status, item quantities across fulfillment stages, revenue calculations, period-over-period comparisons, and the capture timestamp. Used by admin observability dashboards to track business trends, fulfillment rates, and operational efficiency.
IEcommerceMallOrderLifecycleMetric.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from ecommerce_mall_orders and ecommerce_mall_order_items tables. All metrics are calculated dynamically based on time window parameters:
1. order_count: COUNT(DISTINCT order.id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL within time window
2. status_distribution: COUNT(orders) GROUP BY overall_status with filters for paid/shipped/delivered/cancelled/refunded/partiallyCompleted
3. item_metrics: SUM(order_items.quantity) GROUP BY item_status for paid/shipped/delivered/cancelled/refunded
4. price_metrics: SUM(orders.total_price) for total_revenue, AVG(orders.total_price) for average_order_value
5. period_comparison: Calculate delta between current and previous time window; status_change_breakdown tracks orders that transitioned between statuses (paid->shipped, shipped->delivered, delivered->refunded, cancelled)
6. snapshot_at: Current server timestamp when metrics were captured
All calculations exclude soft-deleted records. Timestamps normalized to ISO 8601 UTC.

id.description: Unique identifier for the seller shop profile.
id.x-autobe-specification: UUID - unique identifier for this seller shop profile record. Auto-generated by the database on profile creation.

shopName.description: Name of the seller's shop. Required field, maximum 100 characters.
shopName.x-autobe-specification: Required text field, maximum 100 characters. Must be unique across all seller profiles. This is the public-facing name of the seller's shop.

shopDescription.description: Optional description of the seller's shop. Null if not provided.
shopDescription.x-autobe-specification: Nullable text field. Optional description that can be null if the seller has not provided a shop description. Maximum 5000 characters as per requirements.

logoUrl.description: URL of the seller's shop logo image. Null if logo not uploaded.
logoUrl.x-autobe-specification: Nullable URI field. URL pointing to the shop logo image, or null if no logo has been uploaded by the seller.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the seller profile was created.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Timestamp (timestamptz) when this seller profile was initially created. Auto-generated by the database on profile creation.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the seller profile was last updated.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Timestamp (timestamptz) of the last update to this seller profile. Updated automatically by the database on each profile modification.

IEcommerceMallSellerProfile.ISummary.description: Lightweight seller shop profile summary for administrative dashboards and approval reviews. Contains essential shop identification and branding information including shop name, optional description, and logo image URL. Used when viewing seller profiles in admin interfaces or evaluating seller access requests.
IEcommerceMallSellerProfile.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Seller shop profile summary for administrative dashboards and approval reviews. This type is used for seller shop profile display in administrative dashboards and approval reviews. Properties: id (UUID - unique profile identifier), shopName (required text, max 100 chars - unique shop name), shopDescription (nullable text - optional shop description), logoUrl (nullable URI - shop logo URL or null), createdAt (timestamptz - profile creation timestamp), updatedAt (timestamptz - last profile update timestamp). Security: password_hash from seller table never exposed. Compositions excluded: all has-many relations (products, shipments) per ISummary lightweight design. Used in admin request reviews to provide business context when super administrators evaluate seller privilege escalation requests. Note: databaseSchema set to null as ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles table is not available in loaded schemas.

IEcommerceMallAdminRequestRequestStatus.description: Enumeration of administrator access request approval statuses representing the three possible states in the admin request lifecycle.
IEcommerceMallAdminRequestRequestStatus.x-autobe-specification: String enum with three values representing admin request approval status. Values: 'pending' (awaiting super admin review), 'approved' (granted), 'rejected' (denied). Used for filtering in admin request list queries.

cart_id.description: The unique identifier of the shopping cart containing this cart item.
cart_id.x-autobe-specification: References the shopping cart session from ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id. This identifies the cart where the cart item resides. Computed from the cart parameter passed to the update operation.

cart_item_id.description: The unique identifier of the cart item to update.
cart_item_id.x-autobe-specification: References the specific cart item from ecommerce_mall_cart_items.id. This identifies the exact cart item within the cart whose quantity should be updated. Computed from the cart item parameter passed to the update operation.

quantity.description: The new quantity for the cart item.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: The new quantity value to set for this cart item. Must be a positive integer (> 0). Business rules: quantity must not exceed available stock. Operation executed within ACID transaction to ensure consistency. This is the update target value, not a stored database column.

IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.description: Cart management operation to update the quantity of an existing cart item. Specifies which cart item to update and the new quantity value. Used as part of batch cart operations.
IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.x-autobe-specification: Computation DTO for cart quantity update operation within batch cart management. Contains: cart_id referencing ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id (the cart session), cart_item_id referencing ecommerce_mall_cart_items.id (the specific cart item), quantity as the new quantity value (positive integer). Business rules: quantity must be > 0, must not exceed available stock. Operation executed within ACID transaction to ensure consistency.

variant_id.description: Unique identifier of the product variant to remove from the shopping cart.
variant_id.x-autobe-specification: Operation parameter identifying the product variant UUID to remove. Maps to cart_items.variant_id FK for lookup and deletion within ACID transaction.

IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.description: Request body for removing a product variant from a customer's shopping cart. Specifies the variant identifier for cart item deletion within cart management operations.
IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for shopping cart remove operation. Identifies variant to remove from cart items. Used within IManageOperation to perform batch cart item deletions in ACID transactions. Data source: operation payload, validated against cart_items where variant_id matches target variant UUID.

cart_id.description: The shopping cart ID to synchronize.
cart_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id. UUID format. References the shopping cart session being synchronized.

variant_id.description: The product variant ID to synchronize.
variant_id.x-autobe-specification: References ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id. UUID format. This is a cross-table reference to the product variant whose quantity will be synchronized in the cart. Not a property of the cart table itself.

quantity.description: The target quantity for the variant in the cart.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Integer value for ecommerce_mall_cart_items.quantity. Represents the target quantity for the variant in the cart. Minimum value is 1. This is a cart item attribute, not a direct cart property.

IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.description: Synchronize a product variant's quantity in a shopping cart to a specific known value. This operation is used for conflict resolution and state recovery scenarios.
IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.x-autobe-specification: Sync cart operation that sets variant quantity to a known value for conflict resolution and state recovery. Mappings: cart_id references ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id, variant_id references ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id (cross-table), quantity is integer for cart_items. Uses atomic transaction to ensure variant quantity update is consistent. This is a management operation, not a standard CRUD.

id.description: Unique product variant identifier.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id.

skuCode.description: Stock keeping unit code for the variant.

stockQuantity.description: Current stock quantity available (1-9 units indicating low stock status).
stockQuantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_product_variants.stock_quantity. Minimum value 1 in schema.

productName.x-autobe-specification: Computed via join from ecommerce_mall_product_variants.product to ecommerce_mall_products.name. This is a cross-table join, not a direct column mapping.

sellerId.description: Identifier of the seller who owns this product.
sellerId.x-autobe-specification: Computed via join from ecommerce_mall_product_variants.product to ecommerce_mall_products.seller_id. This is a cross-table join, not a direct column mapping.

IEcommerceMallInventoryHealthMetric.IVar.description: Summary view of a product variant with critical low stock information, including current stock level and product context for prioritized reorder planning.
IEcommerceMallInventoryHealthMetric.IVar.x-autobe-specification: Computed health metric DTO from ecommerce_mall_product_variants joined with ecommerce_mall_products. Fields: id from product_variants.id, skuCode from product_variants.sku_code, stockQuantity from product_variants.stock_quantity, productName from products.name via product relation, sellerId from products.seller_id via product relation. Filter: stock_quantity < 10 AND stock_quantity > 0. Ordered by stock_quantity ascending. This is a summary/metric view not a full entity representation.

variant_id.description: The unique identifier of the product variant to add to the cart.
variant_id.x-autobe-specification: References ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id FK column that will be stored in cart_items.variant_id. Must reference an existing active product variant. The variant's current stock level and price are validated/checked at operation time when creating the cart item record.

quantity.description: The number of variant units to add to the cart. Must be at least 1.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Maps to cart_items.quantity column. Integer field storing the number of variants to add. Must be at least 1. If the same variant already exists in the cart, this operation increments the existing quantity by this amount (aggregate behavior).

IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.description: Request body for adding a product variant to a customer's shopping cart. Specifies which variant to add and the quantity. When submitted, this operation either adds a new cart item or merges with an existing cart item for the same variant by incrementing the quantity.
IEcommerceMallShoppingCart.IManageOperat.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for the IManageOperationAdd cart operation. This is an operation request schema (not a direct entity mapping). variant_id references an existing product variant from ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id and will be stored in cart_items.variant_id FK. quantity specifies the number of variants to add and will be stored in cart_items.quantity. The active cart context (ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts) is resolved from JWT token/actor authentication. Business rules enforced: quantity must be at least 1, variant_id must reference an existing active product variant, stock availability validated at operation time. The operation adds the variant to the customer's cart with the specified quantity, or increments quantity if the same variant already exists in the cart (aggregate behavior).

alert_type.description: Type of system health alert indicating what metric exceeded thresholds.
alert_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed alert classification: error_rate (errors exceeding threshold) or performance_degraded (performance metrics below acceptable level). Derived from audit log analysis and metric aggregation.

action_type.description: The audit action category associated with this alert.
action_type.x-autobe-specification: References the action_type field from audit log entries. Indicates which system operation or audit category triggered the health alert.

current_rate.description: The current metric value that exceeded the defined threshold.
current_rate.x-autobe-specification: The actual numeric value that triggered the alert (percentage, error count, or performance metric). Computed from real-time metric aggregation. Minimum 0.

threshold.description: The threshold value that was exceeded to trigger this alert.
threshold.x-autobe-specification: The limit that was exceeded to trigger this alert. Derived from alert configuration: 1.0 for yellow severity, 5.0 for red severity, 50.0 for performance degradation. Minimum 0.

severity.description: Severity level of the alert indicating urgency: yellow for moderate issues, red for critical issues.
severity.x-autobe-specification: Computed from current_rate vs threshold comparison: yellow for moderate exceedance (>1% of threshold), red for critical exceedance (>5% of threshold). Derived enum from alert severity rules.

message.description: Human-readable description of the alert condition, auto-generated.
message.x-autobe-specification: Auto-generated human-readable message based on alert_type, severity, and threshold exceeded. Computed at alert generation time with template: "{alert_type} exceeded threshold: {current_rate}% (threshold: {threshold}%)". Nullable if message generation fails.

timestamp.description: When the alert was triggered, in ISO 8601 UTC format.
timestamp.x-autobe-specification: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the alert was triggered. Computed from system clock at alert evaluation time. Nullable if timestamp generation fails.

IEcommerceMallSystemHealthMetric.IAlert.description: System health alert triggered when error rates or performance metrics exceed defined thresholds. Provides administrators with actionable information about system issues including the affected operation, current metric value, threshold exceeded, and severity level.
IEcommerceMallSystemHealthMetric.IAlert.x-autobe-specification: Computed alert schema derived from system health monitoring aggregations. alert_type and severity are enum-derived from threshold comparisons. action_type references audit log actions. current_rate and threshold are numeric metrics from observability dashboard calculations. message and timestamp are auto-generated based on alert state. This schema does not map to a single database table.
